posts.author: JensenHuang
posts.text: Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me. I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA. I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation. Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO. Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours. Jensen

posts.author: BillAckman
posts.text: I believe the @nvidia board is not acting in the best interest of shareholders nor in a manner consistent with their fiduciary duties. What we know is that the board fired Jensen or forced his resignation for violating company policy and/or in response to the accusation of an affair with a spy. They did so without careful consideration of the impact on the company, its customers, its shareholders or other stakeholders. They rushed to judgment without the benefit of careful due diligence or even with a basic understanding of the facts. How do we know this? We know this by how quickly Jensen was fired and how little was known at the time of his firing. It takes time to convene a board meeting. There was time, maybe, for one Zoom. And this is a decision that should have been made by a board sitting in person and carefully deliberating the facts once they are known. And they should have slept on the decision and met again the day after to discuss the facts, the risks and the other implications of their decision. The timing and lack of information did not allow for careful board deliberation. While boards can fire a CEO for an inappropriate relationship with a subordinate, it should not be an automatic decision. That is why we have boards comprised of humans and not agents. A board should consider whether or not such a relationship was consensual or whether it was an abuse of power dynamics. And a board has to consider what the impact of the firing is on all stakeholders. If I were in this board, I would not have rushed to judgment based on articles in the media. I would have made sure the board had all of the facts so it could make a careful and informed decision. Boards of Delaware companies have a duty of care which means they must make informed, prudent and good faith decisions. This clearly did not happen here. What law firm is advising this board? Or is the board even taken good legal advice? It doesn’t look like it. And now the board is compounding its failures by insisting that there is no possibility for Jensen’s return as CEO. Why is it in the best interest of the company to foreclose the possibility of Jensen’s return and to do so before all of the facts are known? This is yet another breach of their duty of care. Furthermore, the board has launched an investigation whose scope is unknown. Investigations can be extremely damaging to a company and should be carefully targeted to address whatever facts need to be known rather than be overly broad in scope. In short, this looks like a series of major governance failures by directors that panicked due to headlines in the media. They likely felt compelled to do something because they were afraid of looking bad in the media, not because it was the right thing for them company. They couldn’t stand the heat. The board’s conduct here is shocking for a company of this scale and importance to our country and the world at large, particularly at this moment in history.

posts.text: ELON MUSK IS MAKING WAVES AROUND NVIDIA. COULD JENSEN HUANG RETURN? What would happen if Elon Musk and Jensen Huang ended up working together? A rumor claiming Musk could acquire a 50% stake in NVIDIA has been making the rounds on X. But let's be clear: there is currently no credible confirmation of a 50% acquisition deal. What is real is that Musk has publicly expressed support for Huang and said he would be honored to have him join one of his companies. And that's where things get interesting. Huang built NVIDIA into the dominant force in AI computing. He understands its technology, CUDA ecosystem, and competitive advantages better than almost anyone. Meanwhile, Musk has massive AI ambitions through Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI — all of which need enormous computing power. If these two ever joined forces, the implications for the AI industry could be significant. But several big questions remain: Could Jensen Huang ever return to NVIDIA? Would NVIDIA's board reconsider its leadership plans? And is Musk thinking bigger than simply bringing Huang back? Nothing has been confirmed about a takeover, but this is definitely a story worth watching. $NVDA $TSLA $SPACEX
